glyph_groups.exception_failed_on: criterion 1 - nothing visible on the profile page names status before the tap (only a small green dot); criterion 4 - a first-time user expects the avatar to do what it does everywhere else (open the profile / change the picture), not a status menu
glyph_groups.evidence: the avatar in the bottom account panel (screens 1, 2, 14, 26-35) opens the own-profile page; the same avatar at the top of the profile page (screens 7, 8, 19, 20) opens "Change Online Status". Same picture, same visual state (online dot), unrelated jobs.
glyph_groups.recommendation: give "change status" its own visible control on the profile page (e.g. a "Set status" chip next to the status dot) and keep the avatar's job the same everywhere, or label the profile avatar with visible text naming the status menu

from a candidate: confirmed by tapping all 14 members. Two renderings of "go back": an X on the full-screen profile (a page presented over the app, dismissed rather than navigated) and a left arrow on pushed screens. Justification: different surfaces with different conventions (Phase 3: surface) - an X that closes a full-screen overlay and an arrow that steps back are both first-time mobile conventions, and closing the overlay lands where the user came from, so a user who learned the arrow still finds a way out on the profile. No co-occurrence.

from a candidate: confirmed by tapping all 13 members. The bare magnifier (Messages header) and the magnifier inside a pill with the word "Search" (server header) both open search scoped to their own place. The shared magnifier is a first-time convention and the server version adds the word, so it is more explicit, not less (Phase 3: explicitness, scope).
